Simulation results

Every Python simulation used to design and check the Lab 8 firmware, re-run with the current firmware settings. Team: Gowri Ramaprasad, Derek Weissinger, Owen Crawley. Compiled 2026-10-27.

Summary1 Estimator2 Yaw drift3 Controller & wheel failure 4 Momentum limit5 DEMO SPIN6 DEMO LEVELLimitations
How these were done. Each study runs a Python copy of the firmware code (filter, controller, wheel allocation, demo logic, wheel-command limits) against a separate truth model: a rigid body with four reaction wheels, integrated with rotation matrices rather than the quaternions the firmware uses, so a sign or frame mistake in the firmware maths can't hide in the simulation. Sensor noise uses the values measured on our BNO085 (gyro 2.17×10⁻⁴ rad/s/√Hz). Study 2 instead feeds real logged sensor data through the filter. Model values: table inertia 0.0623 kg·m² (our model), wheel inertia 3.06×10⁻⁴ kg·m², gains ωₙ = 2 rad/s, ζ = 0.9, wheel limit 60 rad/s.

1. Attitude estimator (MEKF) against an independent truth model

originally ekf_check.py, 2026-10-02 Six motion cases, 120 s each after a 60 s calibration, all with gyro bias on every axis. The filter's attitude is compared with the truth model's every 10 ms.

CaseMax roll error (°)Max pitch error (°)Max yaw error (°)
Level, still, no bias0.0510.0560.43
Tilted 10°/−5°, still0.0500.0510.46
Still, gyro bias on all axes0.0510.0560.43
Roll swinging ±0.2 rad/s0.0490.0560.47
Yaw spin 0.55 rad/s (demo rate)0.0610.0460.43
Combined 3-axis motion0.0630.0430.45
Takeaway. Roll and pitch meet ±1° by a factor of ~15 in every case, including a 0.55 rad/s spin. Yaw error (0.4° after 2 min here) comes entirely from the calibration's z-bias error (0.0028 °/s in this run, about 10 °/h). The filter can't correct it, because gravity carries no heading information.

2. Yaw drift vs calibration: replay of logged static data

originally ekf_replay.py, 2026-10-16; extended 2026-10-27 Real gyro and accelerometer data from two static tests (IMU fixed, 37 and 29 min) replayed through the current filter, with the calibration taken from different windows of the same log.

Correction to an earlier figure. We have been quoting "≈3 °/h after warm-up". Across both logs and every calibration window starting 7+ minutes after power-on, the drift is +1 to +8.5 °/h (before warm-up: -7 to -1 °/h). The gyro's bias keeps wandering slowly after warm-up, so a calibration is only as good as the next ~10 minutes. At ~5 °/h, yaw stays within ±1° for about 12 minutes; a 5-minute heading-hold test is fine, but longer runs need a heading reference (magnetometer). The "≈3 °/h" statements in CLAUDE.md, PROGRESS_LOG.md and the prelim deck should be updated.

3. Attitude hold, wheel allocation and a failed wheel

originally ctrl_sim.py, 2026-10-06 ARM-style hold of level, heading 0, from a 5°/−3°/4° start. Three variants: all four wheels; wheel C disabled from the start; wheel C failing 1 s into the manoeuvre.

Takeaway. The minimum-norm allocation over the remaining three wheels reproduces the same body torque, so a wheel loss that is detected costs nothing in pointing; it only loads the remaining wheels harder. This is the basis for requirement 3. The detection itself isn't built yet, and here the simulation is told which wheel failed. A table 2× heavier than the model (0.13 kg·m²) still settles, in 4.1 s.

4. The momentum limit: a steady disturbance

originally ctrl_sim.py, 2026-10-06 The same hold with a constant external torque of 2 mN·m (roll) and −1 mN·m (pitch), like an imbalanced table.

Takeaway. Reaction wheels store momentum; they can't remove it. Hold time ≈ storage ÷ disturbance (26 mN·m·s ÷ 2 mN·m = 13 s, as simulated). This predicted the first DEMO SPIN aborts on the air bearing and is why table balance matters so much: on the table the measured torque went from ≈ 8 mN·m (1–2 s holds) to 1.3 mN·m after trimming (15.8 s hold), matching this relation.

5. The full DEMO SPIN

originally demo_sim.py / demo_sim_bias.py, 2026-10-15/16 Level from a 25°/−20°/40° start, spin up over 10 s, hold 10 s, spin down 10 s, settle, with the 100 rpm null-mode wheel bias.

Takeaway. The demo logic works as designed against the model, and without the wheel bias the target would be 6.37 rpm. But the spin rate is sized from the model inertia (0.0623 kg·m²). With the table 28% heavier, which matches our air-bearing fits for yaw (0.074–0.082 kg·m²), the wheels hit the 55 rad/s abort during spin-up and the demo spins down early. Before the next DEMO SPIN, set the yaw inertia in control_params.h to ≈ 0.08 kg·m²: the target rate then drops to about 4.1 rpm with the same 20% margin.

6. DEMO LEVEL: holding the natural rest tilt

2026-10-27 One axis of a pendulum table (3.3 s swing, rest at −0.5°, as measured after balancing), starting 2° from rest, with the firmware gains. Compared: a roll/pitch reference that slowly follows the measured tilt, versus damping only (reference = measured tilt).

ApproachMomentum stored (mN·m·s)Settle to ±0.25° (s)
reference follows tilt, 4 s4211.0
reference follows tilt, 2 s256.1
reference follows tilt, 1 s173.7
reference follows tilt, 0.5 s122.4
damping only (chosen)81.4
Takeaway. A slowly following reference makes the controller fight gravity while it catches up, which can store more momentum than a pair of wheels holds (~20 mN·m·s). Damping only stores the least (about Kd × the tilt change) and settles fastest. The firmware's DEMO LEVEL now uses damping only on roll/pitch while holding heading. With no steady roll/pitch torque left, the hold should be limited by the ≈ 0.12 mN·m yaw torque: an estimated 6–7 minutes. Not yet tested on the table.

Limitations

  • Inertia is a model. Studies 1, 3, 4 and 5 use 0.0623 kg·m²; the air-bearing fits give 0.05–0.13 (x/y) and 0.074–0.082 (z). Study 3 and 5 include heavier-table variants.
  • No gravity in the 3-axis studies. Studies 3–5 model a perfectly balanced table (except the deliberate torque in study 4). Study 6 adds the pendulum, but in one axis only.
  • Idealised wheels. The speed loop is modelled as a torque-limited first-order response; motor friction, wheel A's rub, wheel C's oscillation and pack sag are not modelled.
  • Sensor model. White gyro noise plus a constant bias; the real bias wander (study 2) and the BNO085's occasional 60–90 ms output stalls are not in studies 1, 3–5.
  • Failure detection is not simulated: study 3 tells the controller which wheel failed.

Scripts: sim_suite.py, replay_cal.py, replay_windows.py, make_sim_figs.py (Claude's working folder; not yet in the repo). Figures: Reports/figures/sim1–sim6.
